rich_summary: Nala confronts his brother Pushkara in a final game of dice after hearing him boast that he will win Damayanti. Though enraged, Nala restrains himself and plays. In a single decisive throw he wins back his wealth, kingdom, and even Pushkara’s staked life. Instead of taking revenge, Nala reveals that his earlier downfall was due to the influence of Kali and magnanimously forgives his brother, restoring him to life and granting him a portion of the kingdom. Damayanti returns from her father Bhima’s court, and Nala resumes joyful rule. The sage Vrihadaswa ends the tale by reminding Yudhishthira that fortune and misfortune are fickle; Nala’s story should comfort him during exile. He then offers to teach Yudhishthira the science of dice, turning the tale into a moral lesson about patience, destiny, and recovery after ruin.

Nala, victorious yet calm, lifting his defeated brother Pushkara and granting him life and forgiveness before the court.
